checks: FR-DOC-019 and REL-DOC-009 separate file publication from authoritative metadata/job commit and queued acknowledgement; published files survive indexing failure or cancellation.

REL-DOC-009 requires bounded body-free private intent with schema, checksum, ordering, root identity, contained locator and hash, lossless original provenance or contained private manifest reference, and metadata that cannot be restored byte-equivalently from final frontmatter.

The sole SQLite owner assigns and durably commits desired revision; accepted intent replay is idempotent; old terminal jobs cannot clear a newer desired revision; dirty and keyword_dirty retain retry state.
FR-DOC-033 preserves completed imported documents and their identity, aliases and metadata across later import failure or cancellation; FR-DOC-019 preserves the legacy journal recovery adapter.

DR-DOC-014 keeps 1:N original aliases and lexical/canonical original paths separate from documents.relative_path, while DR-DOC-013 keeps source-relative identity distinct. Generated documents do not invent origins; FR-DOC-036 keeps resolver and search read-only with verified copy fallback.

FR-DOC-028's existing index_enqueue_failed warning remains required for generic enqueue failure. indexing_ingress_capacity is additive only for private ingress capacity and does not replace index_enqueue_failed.
